newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa dives after new law report.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa dives after new law report.

text.p: Shares in German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG fell sharply in early bourse trade on Tuesday as dealers worried about the impact of a new draft law on the company and the possibility of a capital increase this year.
Lufthansa shares were down five percent or 1.10 marks at 20.75 marks at 1009 GMT while the broader market was steady.

Earlier, after the government issued details of a new draft law for airline share ownership, Lufthansa said it expected the government to sell its Lufthansa stake in the last quarter of 1997 and said no decision had been taken on a rights issue.

Foreign players were particularly worried about the impact on their holdings in Lufthansa of the draft law, which stipulates, among other things, that Lufthansa be allowed to force foreign investors to sell their shares should their holdings in the national airline exceed 50 percent.
They were also concerned about Lufthansa's statement that it expected its shares would have to be converted into non-freely transferable stock.
"The whole deal is making people less sure of the company," said a trader at Deutsche Bank in London.
A Frankfurt trader said he could not understand why there was so much pressure on Lufthansa because of the news.

"I think the risk of a capital increase is one issue and that I can understand but I think that a lot of foreign investors will simply not understand the concept of non-freely transferable shares," he said.
The German government currently owns 36 percent of Lufthansa.
